_about: NYBG staff in their own words: short passages about how the Garden manages a species, copied word for word from a published web page, with the page, its author and date. Typed by hand like content/id-checklists.json, so check each passage against its page before adding it. Keep each one short (a few sentences) and always link the page. build_species.py attaches these to the species record as `voices`; a species that is only here (not in the Forest Plan or another source) still gets a page, named from `scientific_name` and `common_names`.

voices.title: Steaming the Native Plant Garden
voices.speaker: Michael Hagen, curator of the Rock Garden and Native Plant Garden
text: The beautiful Native Plant Garden opened in 2013, but by 2021 the meadow had succumbed to mugwort pressures.
They decided to try to steam away the mugwort in the fall.
They then seeded with a native Virginia wild rye cover crop to prevent any seeds setting in over the winter.
In the spring, they replanted with native perennial plugs like Monarda fistulosa, Heliopsis, and a mix of native asters.
voices.quote: It's an ongoing process, but one that is exciting

voices.title: In your own garden
voices.speaker: Leslie Coleman, NYBG Plant Information Service
text: Mugwort (Artemisia vulgaris) is a terribly difficult to manage weed and there is no technique or control that has been developed yet that will eradicate it in your yard.
It is considered a prohibited invasive species in the states of New York, New Jersey and Connecticut.
Sticking with the repeated treatments is important for maximum impact.
